title: Anthropic Makes History with Massive $81.3 Billion Wall Street Debut
snippet: Artificial intelligence powerhouse Anthropic stormed the public markets, raising a record-shattering $81.3 billion in its initial public offering at a staggering $1.5 trillion valuation.
content:
NEW YORK — Artificial intelligence startup Anthropic made a thunderous debut on Wall Street, surging 17% on its first day of public trading after completing a record-shattering initial public offering that raised $81.3 billion.

Trading under the ticker symbol ANT, the stock opened at $111.50 per share on the Nasdaq late Thursday morning—well above its $83 IPO price. While shares pared back some of their early gains during afternoon trading, the stock ultimately settled at $97.17, giving the San Francisco-based firm a eye-watering $1.5 trillion valuation.

A Historic Nasdaq Debut

Co-founders Dario Amodei, who serves as CEO, and Daniela Amodei, the company's president, were on hand at the Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square to ring the opening bell. Ahead of the first trade, Dario Amodei stressed that safety must remain front and center as advanced AI models are deployed globally.

Daniela Amodei directly addressed public anxieties surrounding the technology's rapid expansion. "To anyone watching who is uneasy about AI or unsure what it will mean for you—this technology needs you," she told reporters. "Not your trust, not your use, but your voice."

Monumental Growth and Market Expectations

Founded in 2021, Anthropic has experienced a meteoric rise. In its amended S-1 regulatory filing, the company revealed that third-quarter revenue reached $17 billion, representing a staggering 12-fold increase year-over-year. The blockbuster performance previously helped earn Anthropic the title of Yahoo Finance's Company of the Year for 2026.

With its high-stakes debut now in the books, investors and Wall Street analysts will closely monitor how effectively the AI leader can maintain its astronomical growth rate while navigating safety, regulatory, and technical challenges in the years ahead.
